u0: The agent is in a clear, normal condition: no freshly fallen box is awaiting an immediate pickup, and the exit has not been reached empty-handed. The remaining obligations are to respond to any future fall by holding the box on the very next step, and to be carrying the box by the time the exit is reached. If the agent is already at the exit holding the box with no fall on that step, both requirements are met. Putting the box down during ordinary travel creates no immediate deadline by itself, but the box must be back in hand when the exit is reached.
u1: A box fall has just happened, so the agent is under an immediate recovery deadline: the box must be in hand on the very next step. If that next step ends with the box held, and with the exit reached while carrying if this is the exit step, the pending pickup is cleared and the normal clear condition is restored. If the box is not held on that next step, the required pickup has been missed and the task fails.
u2: The agent has reached the exit without the box in hand, with no fresh fall pending at that moment. The requirement to be carrying the box when reaching the exit is therefore unmet; arriving at the exit alone does not satisfy the task. If play could continue, taking the box into hand would clear this exit condition; otherwise the condition remains outstanding.
u3: The exit-carriage requirement is already outstanding, and a box fall has just occurred, so two obligations are pending together. The agent must end the very next step holding the box; doing so clears both the immediate recovery and the exit-carriage issue. If the box is not held on that next step, the missed pickup becomes an irreversible failure.
u4: A box fall was not followed by the agent holding the box on the very next step. The required immediate recovery has been missed, so the task can no longer be completed successfully. If the exit was also involved, the requirement to be carrying the box there is unmet as well.
